subject: research/radar-clutter-twin
professional: a radar signal-processing engineer / detection theorist who has designed CFAR processors and refereed work on K-distributed sea clutter (Richards, Skolnik, Watts, Ward school). They would check first that the CA-CFAR threshold formula and the K-clutter false-alarm law are right, then whether iid-per-cell texture is a realistic setting for the headline failure, whether the repair is costed in detection loss, and what the work adds beyond the K-clutter CFAR-loss literature

evidence.correctness: Ran everything and recomputed with scratch scripts that do not import radar_clutter_twin (numpy only, own RNG, seed 20261109; scipy not installed). (1) Threshold formula: alpha = N(Pfa^(-1/N) - 1) for N=16 gives 5.336 / 12.452 / 21.942 at 1e-2 / 1e-4 / 1e-6, the CA-CFAR multiplier of Richards (Fundamentals of Radar Signal Processing, CA-CFAR for square-law detection) and Rohling 1983; matches results.txt and the whitepaper. (2) Real Pfa under iid gamma texture: direct Monte Carlo (8e6 trials, no conditioning) at design 1e-2 gives 0.03025 (nu=2) and 0.01952 (nu=5) against the library's exact 0.03026 and 0.01951; shared texture gives 0.01012 / 0.00994, so the 'ratio test cancels shared texture' claim holds. (3) Conditional Monte Carlo of the speckle-integrated product (1e7 draws, own implementation, standard errors 1e-7 to 2e-5): inflation 30.11 (nu=2), 9.16 (nu=5), 2.38 (nu=20) at 1e-4 and 358.1 / 50.29 / 4.86 at 1e-6, against 30.13 / 9.16 / 2.37 and 358.42 / 50.21 / 4.86 in results.txt, all within about 1 percent. (4) Asymptotic constant: I re-derived it independently (large alpha: g(s) ~ E[1/tau]/s = nu/((nu-1)s), E[tau0^N] = Gamma(nu+N)/(Gamma(nu) nu^N)) and got Gamma(nu+N)/(Gamma(nu)(nu-1)^N) = 2.360e7 (nu=5) and 294.50 (nu=20), the stated values. (5) Moment ratio E[P^2]/E[P]^2 = 2(1+1/nu): simulated 2.397 vs 2.4 at nu=5. (6) Off-grid robustness of the quadrature, compared with my conditional Monte Carlo at design 1e-3: nu=0.5 0.02916 vs 0.02924, nu=1.5 0.01192 vs 0.01193, nu=50 0.0012683 vs 0.0012681, nu=1000 0.010127 vs 0.010131; only nu=0.3 is off, by 1.7 percent (0.0393 vs 0.0400, texture grid truncated at log tau = -12). `experiments/run.py` rerun (about 2.5 min): output byte-identical to experiments/results.txt. Every headline number reproduces; no wrong number found. Silent bad outputs only on out-of-contract inputs (see craft).
evidence.completeness: Claims in README/whitepaper checked: exact one-dimensional Pfa law matches Monte Carlo (reproduced, tests + run.py section 2); design 1e-2 -> 0.030 (nu=2) and 0.020 (nu=5) (reproduced); 9x-30x at 1e-4 and 50x-358x at 1e-6 (reproduced); asymptotic limit verified numerically (reproduced, 1.001 of limit at alpha=1e6); repair costs 1.9 dB (nu=5) to 3.7 dB (nu=2) at 1e-4 (results.txt section 3 matches, not independently recomputed beyond the Pfa function it inverts); shared texture 0.0101 vs 0.0100 (reproduced); moment-fit median 1.1x at n=1000 (results.txt shows 1.12 and 1.15, p90 2.06 and 2.16, consistent with the README's 'p90 still 2x'); 'small n (<=300) worse than useful' (p90 3.3-9.6 at n=100-300: consistent). '8 tests, ~15 s': 8 tests ran, 6 s. Files exist: paper/whitepaper.md, experiments/{run.py,figure.py,results.txt,pfa_inflation.svg}. No TODO or stub. The live page https://marisstella.app/research/radar-clutter-twin/ was not loaded (proxy). evidence.verification: `cd research/radar-clutter-twin; PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m unittest discover -s tests`: Ran 8 tests, OK, 6 s. The tests are not purely self-referential: the exact law is checked against a direct Monte Carlo, the asymptotic constant against the quadrature at alpha=1e6, the estimator against simulated data, the root-finder by round trip. Two hand-seeded mutations in src/radar_clutter_twin/model.py, each reverted with `git checkout` (git status clean under the project afterwards): (1) nu_moment_estimate divisor 2 -> 2.1 (a 5 percent bias in the nu fit): CAUGHT (test_moment_estimator_consistent, 1.154 vs 1.0 within 0.12). (2) TextureGrid default ylo -12.0 -> -3.0 (the quadrature drops the low-texture tail that dominates the false alarms at small design Pfa): NOT caught, 8/8 pass, because the exact-law test is only at design 1e-2 and the 1e-4 tests (alpha_for_pfa round trip, recalibration with true nu) use the same grid on both sides. So a corrupted tail integral at the deep-tail Pfa that the paper is about would pass. No test pins results.txt (run.py has no assertions; agreement is read by eye); no test for nu <= 1, N other than 16, or invalid Pfa.
evidence.craft: Read src/radar_clutter_twin/model.py (131 lines), tests/test_model.py, experiments/run.py, pyproject.toml, README and whitepaper. The module is compact, stdlib-only, with docstrings that state the derivation (speckle integrated out analytically, then 1-D quadrature over the cell-under-test texture and a tabulated g(s) = E[1/(1+s tau)]); deterministic seeds; GridCache avoids rebuilding grids. Defects found by running it: (a) alpha_twin(2.0, 16) silently returns -0.678 (Pfa > 1 accepted) and alpha_twin(0, N) raises a bare ZeroDivisionError; (b) pfa_real(0, ...) raises 'math domain error' from math.log(0) in gfun; (c) inflation_limit(nu <= 1) raises 'math domain error' (the limit is infinite for nu <= 1, documented in the docstring as 'for nu > 1' but not guarded); (d) TextureGrid has fixed quadrature bounds (log tau in [-12, 4], 320 points) with no check: accurate for nu from about 0.5 to 1000 in my comparison, 1.7 percent low at nu=0.3, with no warning; (e) alpha_for_pfa brackets alpha in [1e-6, 1e9] and returns the upper bracket silently if the target is unreachable (alpha_for_pfa(1e-30, 16, nu=2) = 8823, not flagged as grid-limited); (f) calibration_trials clamps nu_hat at 0.6 and recalibrated_pfa reverts to the Gaussian twin above 200, both disclosed. __all__ in __init__ via star import is acceptable for a small research package. run.py has hard-coded numbers, no CLI, no asserts.
evidence.claims: Checked each README/whitepaper claim against results.txt and my recomputation (see completeness and correctness); each is backed and reproduces. Limits are stated in the first paragraph and in the whitepaper 'Limitations' (stylised, single-pulse square law, iid unit-mean gamma texture, no target, no real data, correct-family assumption in result 6, binomial rule of thumb for the 1e6-cell figure, 'only Pfa, not Pd'). The 'Builds on' sentence explicitly says no ARPG paper is reproduced and there is no affiliation. Small inaccuracies: (i) Rohling (1983) is the OS-CFAR paper and is cited as a CA-CFAR/detector model source; CA-CFAR theory is Finn & Johnson 1968 and Richards/Skolnik, which Richards is not cited; (ii) the claim 'restoring the design rate costs a 1.9 dB threshold' is a threshold multiplier, not a detection-loss (the whitepaper says so in result 4, the README one-liner does not); (iii) the whitepaper frames 'a twin should model clutter's spatial correlation length, not just its marginal' as a finding, which follows from the model construction (the ratio test cancels a shared factor). The research/README.md index line reproduces the numbers correctly. No disclaimer problem (research, MIT, stylised). Live page not loaded.
evidence.fitness: Research bar (research/CLAUDE.md): multi-session programmes aimed at publishable papers. This is one small session, about 130 lines of model code, 1-D pure-Python quadrature. Nearest prior work: CA-CFAR in K-distributed clutter is a classical topic: Watts (1985, 1987, IEE Proc. F / IEEE Trans. AES, detection in K-distributed sea clutter), Watts and Wicks (1990, CFAR in K clutter), Raghavan (CFAR loss analysis in compound-Gaussian clutter), Sekine and Mao (1990, Weibull Radar Clutter, CFAR loss under Weibull/K), Gini and Farina on CFAR in compound-Gaussian clutter, and Ward (1981) for the clutter model itself; none is cited except Ward. The exact one-dimensional form (speckle integrated out, then expectations over per-cell texture) and the CFAR-loss-in-K-clutter phenomenon are, to my knowledge, known in that literature (from memory, not looked up here); the likely new parts are the closed-form asymptotic inflation constant Gamma(nu+N)/(Gamma(nu)(nu-1)^N), its unreachable-in-practice caveat, and the 'real-cell calibration budget' from a moment fit with an explicit p90 table. Those are sound (I reproduced them) but small, and the sim-to-real 'twin' framing adds a story rather than a method. A researcher could reuse the quadrature as a check on a CFAR simulator, but there is no detection-probability analysis, no OS/GO/CMLD comparison, no real clutter data (IPIX etc.) and no misspecification test, so there is little to build a paper on yet. Scored 2: a correct, honest, partly-known result.
evidence.domain: A senior radar engineer would accept the square-law CA-CFAR model, the exponential-speckle times gamma-texture (K) clutter model, and the threshold multiplier, and would find the numbers right. Where it departs from practice: (1) Texture is drawn independently per range cell, which is the worst case and not how K clutter behaves: in real sea clutter the texture correlation length is long (tens of metres to seconds) compared with a CFAR window at most resolutions, so the window usually sees a mostly shared texture, which the paper itself shows is harmless (0.0101 vs 0.0100). The headline 9x-358x inflation therefore applies only to ultra-high-resolution or fast-decorrelating cases, and the work gives no map from range resolution / correlation length to the interpolation between the two extremes (a partially correlated texture is the realistic case and is not computed). (2) Practitioners handle heavy tails with OS-CFAR, GO/SO-CFAR or log-CFAR/ CFAR-with-shape-parameter, not by raising the CA multiplier; the 1.9-3.7 dB 'repair' is shown without detection loss, so the cost the engineer cares about (Pd at a given SNR) is not known. (3) A Gaussian-clutter 'twin' calibrating a CA-CFAR threshold is a straw man; real design uses Weibull/K fits to measured data (IPIX, Skolnik ch. 5-6 style). (4) The moment fit from E[P^2]/E[P]^2 is the textbook K-parameter estimator but is known to be high-variance; the fourth-moment/ log-moment (z log z) estimators used in practice are not compared. (5) Single-pulse, no thermal noise, no target, no pulse integration (Watts's K+noise results). Signed off as a correct, clearly labelled stylised calculation, not as a design method.

defects.what: The texture-quadrature tail is untested at deep-tail Pfa: replacing TextureGrid ylo=-12 with -3 (dropping the low-texture tail that dominates false alarms at small design Pfa) passes all 8 tests, because the exact-law test is only at design 1e-2 and the 1e-4 tests use the same grid on both sides of the comparison.

Headline false-alarm inflation (9x-358x) rests on texture independent per cell, the worst case; real K clutter has long texture correlation and the paper itself shows shared texture gives no inflation. The realistic partially correlated case is neither computed nor mapped to resolution, so the practical relevance of the headline numbers is unquantified. Also the K-clutter CFAR-loss literature (Watts 1985/1987, Watts and Wicks 1990, Sekine and Mao) is not cited, so novelty is not established.

Input validation: alpha_twin accepts Pfa > 1 and returns a negative multiplier (alpha_twin(2, 16) = -0.678), alpha_twin(0) raises ZeroDivisionError, pfa_real(0, ...) and inflation_limit(nu <= 1) raise a bare 'math domain error', alpha_for_pfa returns its upper bracket silently when the target is below what the grid resolves (alpha_for_pfa(1e-30, 16, nu=2) = 8823), TextureGrid is 1.7 percent low at nu=0.3 without a warning.

Rohling (1983) is the OS-CFAR paper and is listed as a classical detector/clutter model source with Finn and Johnson; a standard CA-CFAR reference (Richards, Skolnik) is absent. README one-liner states a 'threshold' cost in dB without saying it is not detection loss (the whitepaper says so).
experiments/run.py has no assertions or regression check against results.txt; agreement between the exact law and Monte Carlo is read by eye.

verdict: A small, correct, honestly labelled calculation. Every headline number reproduces: I recomputed the CA-CFAR multiplier against the Richards/Rohling formula, the exact Pfa under iid gamma texture by direct and by conditional Monte Carlo in numpy (inflation 30.1/9.16/2.38 at 1e-4 and 358/50.3/4.86 at 1e-6 within 1 percent), the asymptotic inflation constant by an independent derivation, and the moment relation; run.py regenerates results.txt byte for byte and the 8 unit tests pass. The weaknesses are in what it means rather than what it computes: a seeded mutation that truncates the texture quadrature's low tail passes all tests (the other, a 5 percent bias in the nu estimator, was caught), the headline failure assumes per-cell independent texture which the paper itself shows disappears under the shared texture typical of real K clutter, no detection loss or alternative CFAR is evaluated, and the closely related K-clutter CFAR-loss literature (Watts, Watts and Wicks, Sekine and Mao) is not cited, so the novelty is at best the asymptotic constant and the calibration-budget table. Meets the quality bar (correctness 4, claims 3, verification 3, median 3) and is finished against its own stated scope, but is not yet a publishable research result (fitness 2, domain 2).
